column7: The last は is read "wa".
Polite: おはようございます (ohayō gozaimasu).
The last は is read "wa".
Polite: おやすみなさい (oyasuminasai).
Polite: ありがとうございます (arigatō gozaimasu).
For longer partings; friends say じゃあね (jā ne).
Also れい (rei), written 零.
Also し (shi), often avoided because it sounds like "death".
Also しち (shichi).
Also く (ku).
Large numbers are counted in units of 10 000 (まん, man): 20 000 is にまん (niman).
いくらですか (ikura desu ka) = how much is it?
ふくろはいりません (fukuro wa irimasen) = I don't need a bag.
これをください (kore o kudasai) = this one, please.
トイレはどこですか (toire wa doko desu ka) = where is the toilet?
Someone else's father: おとうさん (otōsan).
Someone else's mother: おかあさん (okāsan).
Not おじさん (ojisan), which means uncle.
Not おばさん (obasan), which means aunt.
Also used for green traffic lights.
